One run, no re-delivery, and the reason is visible on the agent's last-attempt text.

design:
Tier 1. No migration, no settings change.
D1. The run's operator waits are tracked in memory, in a new module hub/hub/run_waits.py: begin(run_id, key, until), end(run_id, key) and paused(run_id, now). This is enough because the run and its clock live in this process, and a Hub restart ends both. The ask route that stamps wait_expires_at (api/v1/agent_actions.py, around line 812) begins one wait per blocking question, until = wait_expires_at. Answer, decline, the wait-ended report and the run's end each end it. Copilot's answer_permission brackets request_approval with a begin and an end, until = now + the agent's permission wait. A wait that leaks is harmless: paused() never counts past its until.
D2. _send_and_wait's poll loop (copilot_acp.py:2988) moves the shared deadline forward by each poll interval during which paused() is true, so refusal continuations keep one budget for work.
D3. A deadline cut sets error_kind turn_timeout, and UNRETRYABLE_ERROR_KINDS (copilot_acp.py:980) gains it. return_run_entries' withdrawal reason for turn_timeout names the limit and the advice. Other unretryable kinds keep today's text.

checked: copilot_acp.py:3012 is the only place the deadline failure is written, and it carries no error_kind
copilot_acp.py:3189 maps error_kind to retryable=False through UNRETRYABLE_ERROR_KINDS
inbound_queue.py:401 already withdraws a retryable=False entry after one attempt
run_task_binding.record_wait_ended and the run-end sweep (run_divergence.py:987) only stamp an expired wait
limits: A 600 s drive step takes real minutes: the drive costs about 22 minutes and 2 premium requests

problem: F782 (A): a Copilot turn that reaches the fixed 600 s deadline (`copilot_acp._send_and_wait`, `copilot_acp.py:3012`) fails with no `error_kind`, so `inbound_queue.return_run_entries` (`inbound_queue.py:341`) treats it as a crash and re-delivers it unchanged, twice. The retry note only says an earlier attempt was cut off (`inbound_queue.py:224-227`), so the agent repeats the same long command. Measured: three runs, 30 min 14 s, three premium requests, then the entry was dropped and the operator got no reply. F783 (A): the same clock runs while `ask_user` waits for the operator. A 600 s question wait (`MAX_WAITING_SECONDS`, `api/v1/agents.py:2834`) cannot finish inside a 600 s turn. The run was killed 3 s before the question's own wait ended, the retry asked the same question again, and the operator's answer to the first card queued behind the retry. It reached the agent 9 min 38 s later. Ask me permission cards (`request_approval`, `copilot_acp.py:2585`) consume the same clock.

requirements.rationale: F783: an ask the Hub allows to wait 600 s must fit inside a 600 s turn, and time the operator takes is not the agent's work.
requirements.statement: A Copilot turn's deadline MUST NOT count time its run spends waiting on the operator: from a blocking ask_user question's ask until it is answered, declined or its wait ends, and never past its wait_expires_at; and while an Ask me permission card the run raised is open. The deadline MUST still bound the turn's own work, and every pause MUST end at the wait's own expiry.

requirements.rationale: F782: the same input re-sent after a deadline cut does the same long work and is cut again.
requirements.statement: A Copilot turn that reaches its deadline MUST end failed with error_kind turn_timeout and retryable false. Its input MUST be withdrawn after that one attempt, not re-delivered, and the withdrawn entry's reason MUST name the limit in seconds and say to run long commands in the background or split the work. The run's error MUST state the limit.

in_scope: Copilot turn deadline pauses while the run waits on the operator
a deadline cut is unretryable and withdrawn with a reason naming the limit
non_goals: A per-agent turn-limit setting (F782 expectation 2). It needs an agents column, which is a migration and so Tier 2. It stays open on F782 as its own follow-up.
Codex: it shares DEFAULT_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS but cannot be driven on this machine.

Stamping wait_ended_at on a live question at run end. The Questions route already reads asker_waiting false once the asking run has ended (api/v1/questions.py:457), and a task-bound run's open question parks its task on purpose (run_divergence.py:964). With both requirements below, a deadline cut no longer re-asks.

summary: A Copilot turn's 600 s deadline stops counting while the run waits on the operator (an ask_user question or an Ask me card), and a turn that still reaches the deadline is withdrawn at once with a reason that names the limit, instead of being run twice more unchanged (F782, F783).
